question: Which of the following is the most effective primary prevention strategy against cervical cancer caused by high-risk HPV types?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. HPV vaccination before sexual debut is the most effective primary prevention strategy. The vaccine induces neutralising antibodies against high-risk HPV types 16 and 18 (which cause ~70% of cervical cancers), preventing initial infection of the cervical epithelium.

answers.text: Regular Pap smear screening starting at age 21

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pap smear screening is a secondary prevention strategy — it detects pre-cancerous cervical changes after HPV has already established infection. While critically important for early detection, it does not prevent HPV infection itself.

answers.text: Consistent condom use with every sexual contact

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Condoms reduce HPV transmission by approximately 70% but do not provide complete protection because HPV infects skin areas not covered by the condom (vulva, perineum, perianal region). Condoms are valuable but less effective than vaccination for HPV-specific primary prevention.

answers.text: Prophylactic acyclovir for all sexually active women

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Acyclovir is effective against herpes simplex virus (HSV), not human papillomavirus (HPV). There is no antiviral prophylaxis for HPV — vaccination is the only specific primary prevention strategy.

overallFeedback.feedback: Distinguish primary prevention (preventing infection — vaccination) from secondary prevention (early detection — screening). HPV vaccination before sexual debut is the most effective primary prevention against cervical cancer.

HPV vaccination before sexual debut provides the strongest protection against HPV-related cervical cancer. India recommends vaccination for girls aged 9–14 years as part of the national immunisation strategy.
